title: Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency: First Converted Day after a Return from Another Payer
content:
**Revenue cycle note, returns to private pay — Private Pay Long-Term Care Residency.** The first converted day of the conversion credit — the first day of the advance given back because another payer source covered it — follows how the agreement left the other payer source. The Part A coverage start date is read from the resident's **Medicare Part A Skilled Nursing Facility Coverage** episode whose booked days run latest, its booked block that begins latest deciding.

| Agreement and records | First converted day |
|---|---|
| Active again with Medicare Part A recorded as the payer source it was last converted to, and the Part A coverage start date on or before the last day of the charge's span | The later of that coverage start date and the first day of the span |
| Active again with another payer source recorded as the one it was last converted to, and an earlier charge of the agreement already carrying a payer-conversion credit | The first day of the charge's span |
| Any other case | The later of the conversion date recorded on the agreement and the first day of the charge's span |

**Points of judgement.** Active again with Part A last recorded, but the coverage start falls after the span's last day: third row. Active again after hospice room and board, with a payer-conversion credit on an earlier month's charge: the first day of the span. Still converted, not active again: third row.
